solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Putting bible back, I can't suspect authority of church

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for the bible is to be written the other way round

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the bible

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective meaning dubious, tells us the letters of I CAN'T are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Someone flings a bible down, declaring they cannot trust the church's authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AV into VA; 'suspect' rearranges I CANT to TICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the seat and governing power of the Roman Catholic Church, so it stands for that church's authority.

clue.text: Confirm return of top-class racing with ideal setting

indicators.note: setting means mounting like a jewel, so the ideal word holds the racing piece

parts.note: very means ideal or exact, as in the very thing

indicators.note: return of says the racing abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: F1 is Formula One, top-class motor racing, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Confirm that top-flight motor racing will return to an ideal venue.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 is Formula One, with the figure 1 read as the letter I. 'Ideal' for VERY rests on phrases like 'the very thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify is to establish that something is true, to confirm it.

clue.text: Even risks reversing American vessel into position

indicators.note: reversing means turning back, so the whole combination is read the other way
into says the American vessel is put inside the position word

parts.note: a spot is a position or place
USS, United States Ship, prefixes US navy vessels

explanation.surface: Taking even chances by backing an American warship into position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' sits at the front yet applies to everything after it, container and all, giving SPUSSOT read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is an even chance, as with a coin flip, so even risks are toss-ups.

clue.text: To hit hard, experienced hands move like this

parts.note: to clock someone is slang for hitting them hard
wise means experienced and knowing

explanation.surface: A seasoned boxer's fists strike hard and fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' suggests a boxer's fists, but these are the hands of a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The hands of a clock go round in the direction called clockwise.

clue.text: Not quite intimate

definitions.meaning: ... means almost, as in a ... miss
... means close or intimate, as in ... and dear

explanation.surface: Someone who is almost, but not quite, a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Near means both almost (nearly there) and close in relationship, as in a near relative.

clue.text: 220-yard run with golf shot

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters of run and golf are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A golfer's long shot that then runs on for 220 yards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like the golf noun but is the anagram signal, rearranging RUNGOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlong is an eighth of a mile, exactly 220 yards, still used as a distance in horse racing.

clue.text: Inaccurate piracies of works as published

indicators.note: inaccurate means not right, so the letters of piracies of are not in their correct order

explanation.surface: Pirated editions of books are full of errors compared to the published texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inaccurate' rearranges PIRACIESOF.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair copy is a clean final version of a document, as it stands ready for publication.

clue.text: A German pursuing extremely rich banker locally

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the German word comes after
extremely points to the extremes of rich, its first and last letters

parts.note: ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A German chasing a wealthy banker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is something with banks, a river; 'locally' means as the Germans call it, so the Rhine as Rhein.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhein is the German name of the Rhine, a river and hence a thing with banks.

clue.text: Painting efficiently's a boring source of income?

parts.note: oil is a painting done in oils
well means efficiently or competently

explanation.surface: Is painting efficiently just a dull way to earn a living?
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but means drilling; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil well is a drilled hole that brings up oil, a lucrative earner for its owner.

clue.text: Man's close relative leading parrot

parts.note: great means leading or eminent
to parrot is to mimic, to ape

explanation.surface: A man's nearest relation is a talkative parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' is the verb meaning to copy, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Great apes such as chimpanzees are humanity's nearest living kin in evolution.

clue.text: Nervous crossing peak, in need of a pick-me-up

indicators.note: crossing here means stretching across, so the word for nervous spans the other pieces

parts.note: restive means fidgety or nervous

indicators.note: the peak is in need of the letter A, so A is joined on after it

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, as on Dartmoor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jittery climber crossing a summit badly needs a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervous' tempts as an anagram signal, but it is a synonym, restive.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorative is a tonic or drink that revives you, which is what a pick-me-up is.

clue.text: Old priest first to finish pork pie

indicators.note: the first letter goes to the finish, so the priest's opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: Eli was the priest in the Old Testament who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: An elderly priest is the first to polish off the pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to finish' moves the E of ELI to the end. 'Pork pie' is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie (often shortened to 'porky').
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang pork pie rhymes with, and so means, an untruth.

clue.text: Menial career collecting rubbish Jack disposed of

indicators.note: collecting means gathering something in, so the word for career holds the next piece

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong, to fly

indicators.note: disposed of says the letter for Jack is thrown out of the rubbish word

parts.note: junk is rubbish
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A lowly job collecting rubbish that some fellow called Jack has thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is the verb meaning to rush, not a profession, despite the employment surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A flunky is a servile attendant, a lackey doing menial tasks.

clue.text: European pleased to find info online

parts.note: content means pleased or satisfied

explanation.surface: A European is delighted at finding information on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: E-content is material such as text and media delivered electronically, i.e. information found on the web.

clue.text: A fine feminine capacity for kindliness?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
ability is capacity or power to do something

explanation.surface: Is a fine woman naturally capable of kindness?
explanation.definitionFit: Affability is friendliness and good nature, close in sense to kindliness.

clue.text: Trait shown by English pet tucking into meal with sauce

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the word for pet is placed within the meal

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
a pet is a fit of pique or sulk, as is a tiff
lip is cheek or impudence, as is sauce

explanation.surface: An English pet dog gets stuck into a meal smothered in sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is the old noun for a sulk, and 'sauce' means cheek, not a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff upper lip, stoical restraint in adversity, is the stereotypical national character of the English.

clue.text: Freed from other responsibilities primarily during duty days

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so the picked letters fall inside the duty word

parts.note: excise is a duty or tax on goods

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the initial letters of other and responsibilities are taken

explanation.surface: Someone relieved of other tasks while on duty days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freed' is freed of an evil spirit; 'from' is only a link word, though it reads as part of 'freed from'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exorcised is to be rid of a demon by ritual, i.e. freed of possession.

clue.text: Penalties restricting overseas party funds

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the penalties word holds the party inside it

parts.note: fines are monetary penalties
the ANC is the African National Congress, a South African political party

explanation.surface: Penalties limit how a foreign political party is funded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overseas' is needed because the ANC is South African, not British.
explanation.definitionFit: Finances are monetary resources, the money or funds available to someone.

clue.text: Sharing problems aboard?

parts.note: the idiom for being in the same difficult situation as others is read literally as all being passengers on one vessel

explanation.surface: Fellow passengers on a ship sharing their troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means facing the same difficulties as others; aboard pictures it literally as one shared vessel.

clue.text: Meaner pugilist using wrong side of fist

indicators.note: the word fist has two end letters as sides; the boxer swaps the left one for the right one

parts.note: a pugilist is a boxer, a fighter

explanation.surface: A nastier boxer punches with the wrong side of the fist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using wrong side of fist' replaces F, the first side of FIST, with T, its other side.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight means stingy, so tighter is meaner with money.

clue.text: Extremity one struggles to cut?

indicators.note: to cut means to slice into, so the jumbled one goes inside the extremity word

parts.note: a tail is the extremity or end of something

indicators.note: struggles suggests thrashing about, so the letters of one are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A body part at the end of the foot that is a struggle to trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggles' scrambles the word one into OENA. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: an awkward extremity to clip.
explanation.definitionFit: Toenails grow at the tips of the toes, a bodily extremity, and are awkward to reach and trim.

clue.text: Drug-injecting worker in need of dough's a mug

indicators.note: injecting means putting into, so the drug letter goes inside the worker

parts.note: a baker needs dough to make bread
E is ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A cash-strapped worker who injects drugs is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of dough' suggests being short of money, but dough is bread dough. 'a mug' looks like a dupe, but it is a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaker is a tall drinking cup, essentially a mug.

clue.text: Nothing taken from a month's provision toasted with cheese

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August, a month

indicators.note: taken from says the letter for nothing is removed from the following words

parts.note: a ration is an allowed provision of food
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone's monthly food allowance has been raided and nothing is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' removes O from AUGRATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Au gratin describes a dish with a browned crust of grated cheese or breadcrumbs, grilled until toasted.

clue.text: Record-holder, somewhat egotistical, bumptious

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A record-holding athlete who is rather full of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a sleeve or book holding records, or a record of photographs.

clue.text: Plan second church straddling border

indicators.note: straddling means standing astride, so the church letters sit either side of the border

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A plan for a second church to be built across a boundary line.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a systematic plan or arrangement for achieving something.

clue.text: Fancy man in particular supporting wife

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means holding up from below, so the man comes after the wife

parts.note: him is a particular man, the pronoun for that one

explanation.surface: A woman's lover supports his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' is the down-clue indicator that HIM sits below W. 'Fancy man' looks like a lover, but 'Fancy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim is a sudden fancy or impulse.

clue.text: Queen, say, regularly represented in charts

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of charts is picked out

explanation.surface: The Queen, or perhaps the band Queen, regularly appearing in the hit parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty or the rock band, but a queen is also a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is the term for a female cat, so a queen is an example of the animal.

clue.text: Title adopted by British author's a clever one

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the title sits inside the British and author pieces

parts.note: Muriel Spark was a Scottish novelist
a title is a legal right or claim, as in title to land

explanation.surface: A titled British author is credited with a witty remark.
explanation.walkthrough: Muriel Spark, the Scottish novelist, wrote The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie. 'Title' means a legal claim, not a rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright spark is an informal, often ironic name for a clever, lively person.

clue.text: Rabble drained particularly potent brew

parts.note: a scrum is a disorderly crowd, a rabble

indicators.note: drained means emptied of contents, leaving only the outside letters of particularly

explanation.surface: A rowdy mob has emptied the strong ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained' strips PARTICULARLY to PY. Scrumpy is rough farmhouse cider from the West Country of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is strong, unrefined cider, notoriously potent, brewed on farms in south-west England.

clue.text: Someone sticking nose in fruit, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the fruit's name, when spoken, gives the answer

parts.note: the medlar is a small brown fruit eaten when half rotten

explanation.surface: A nosy person poking their nose into the fruit bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone sticking nose in' reads like a picture of sniffing fruit, but it is the definition of a busybody.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddler interferes in others' affairs, figuratively poking their nose in where unwanted.
